question: When and where was Gaudí born, and when did he die?
reference: Gaudí was born on 25 June 1852 in Reus (though he later claimed the neighbouring village of Riudoms). He died on 10 June 1926 in Barcelona.
contexts:
Antoni Gaudí: Catalan Modernisme (Art Nouveau); considered its greatest exponent, though his mature work transcends the movement, drawing chiefly from natural and geometric forms (ruled surfaces, hyperboloids, catenary arches).  Facts:
Never married; devoted his life entirely to his profession and, from 1915 onward, to the Sagrada Família alone
Rarely drew detailed plans, preferring three-dimensional scale models he shaped as he conceived a design
Died after being struck by a Barcelona tram on 7 June 1926 while walking to daily prayer and confession; because of his shabby dress in later life he was initially mistaken for a beggar and did not receive immediate aid, dying three days later on 10 June 1926
His principal patron was industrialist Eusebi Güell, who commissioned Park Güell, Palau Güell, and the crypt of Colònia Güell, among other major works
Influenced later architects including Le Corbusier, Pier Luigi Nervi, Friedensreich Hundertwasser, Oscar Niemeyer, Félix Candela, Eduardo Torroja, Santiago Calatrava, and Norman Foster
On 11 September 1924 (Catalonia's National Day), Gaudí was beaten at a demonstration against the Catalan language ban and arrested by the Civil Guard while travelling to attend a mass for Catalan patriots; he refused to speak Spanish, insisting he paid his taxes but would not stop speaking his own language, and was released after paying 50 pesetas bail
Introduced the trencadís mosaic technique using broken or waste ceramic pieces, seen on the undulating bench at Park Güell (with Josep Maria Jujol) and the façade of Casa Batlló (with waste from the Pelegrí glassworks)
Emili Sala Cortés was one of Gaudí's professors at the Barcelona architecture school, and Gaudí worked as a draughtsman for him early in his career to help finance his studies; decades later Gaudí was hired to completely redesign Sala Cortés's original 1877 building into Casa Batlló
Dragons were seen as Catalan nationalist symbols during the Renaixença due to their connection with Saint George (patron saint of Catalonia), connecting Casa Batlló's dragon-back roof and Park Güell's dragon/salamander to Gaudí's Catalan identity
answer: Gaudí was born in 1852 in Reus, Catalonia, Spain. He died in 1926 in Barcelona, Spain.

question: In which district of Barcelona is the Sagrada Família located?
reference: The Sagrada Família is a Catholic church under construction in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.
contexts:
Sagrada Família: Gothic Revival combined with curvilinear Art Nouveau / Catalan Modernisme. Still under construction. On 30 October 2025 it became the tallest church building in the world, surpassing Ulm Minster (161.5 m); it reached its full height of 172.5 m on 20 February 2026. The main structure was targeted for completion around 2026 (the centenary of Gaudí's death), but sculptural details, decoration, and a planned monumental stairway are expected to continue until 2034. Funded solely by private donations and visitor entry fees, with no government or church funding. Received 3 million visitors by 1990 and 5 million in 2025. Facts:
As of 30 October 2025, it is the tallest church in the world (172.5 m, ~11 m taller than the former record-holder, Ulm Minster)
Gaudí devoted the rest of his life to the project and is buried in its crypt
At Gaudí's death in 1926, only an estimated 15-25% of the project was complete
In July 1936, anarchists from the FAI set fire to the crypt during the Spanish Civil War and broke into Gaudí's workshop, destroying many of his original plans and models
An arsonist set a small fire in the sacristy in April 2011; investigations later revealed the basilica was an intended target of the 2017 Barcelona (La Rambla) terrorist attacks, a plot that was abandoned after an accidental explosion at the attackers' bomb-making site
Construction halted for the first time since the Civil War when COVID-19 closed the site in March 2020
The interior columns are a unique Gaudí design that branch to support their load, with ever-changing cross-sections created by intersecting geometric forms — for example, a square base evolving into an octagon, then a sixteen-sided shape, and eventually a circle, produced by two helicoidal columns twisting in opposite directions
An organ with 26 stops and 1,492 pipes on two manuals and a pedalboard was installed in the chancel in 2010 by Blancafort Orgueners de Montserrat; additional organs are planned throughout the building, totaling around 8,000 pipes when complete
The Passion façade contains a magic square based on the 1514 print Melencolia I by Albrecht Dürer, modified so its rows, columns, and diagonals add up to 33 (Christ's age at death) instead of the standard 34 for a 4x4 magic square
The central doors of the Glory façade, designed by Josep Maria Subirachs and installed in September 2008, bear the text of the Lord's Prayer in Catalan in high relief, surrounded by the phrase 'give us this day our daily bread' in fifty other languages; the door handles form the letters 'A' and 'G' for Antoni Gaudí
answer: La Sagrada Familia is located in the Eixample district.

question: What is trencadís?
reference: Trencadís is a mosaic technique that Gaudí introduced, using waste or broken ceramic pieces, seen for example on the façade of Casa Batlló and the bench at Park Güell.
contexts: Serpentine Bench (Banc de trencadís) (part of park_guell). Materials: trencadís (broken tile/ceramic/glass mosaic).
